task_instance: Choose the correct SageMaker serving container image URI (and any required deployment flags) for deploying a HuggingFace text-generation LLM, e.g. Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, to a SageMaker endpoint in us-east-1, following the skill's mandated workflow of reading the current tag from AWS's Deep Learning Containers catalog page rather than hardcoding from memory.
blocker_detail: The skill's entire core deliverable (Rule Zero / 'Where image URIs come from' / 'Workflow' sections) requires fetching a live, AWS-maintained catalog page (https://aws.github.io/deep-learning-containers/reference/available_images/) or its GitHub-hosted YAML fallback (raw.githubusercontent.com / api.github.com) or live ECR (`aws ecr describe-images`) to determine the CURRENT image tag/URI, since the skill explicitly forbids hardcoding a URI from memory ('Never hardcode a container URI from memory... Prevents stale-image failures and wrong-region URIs'). This workstation has no network access: curl to aws.github.io was rejected by the local proxy with HTTP 403 (host not in the allowed egress list), confirming no path to the catalog, GitHub, or AWS ECR APIs. `aws` CLI is installed but has no network route and no credentials configured, so `aws ecr describe-images` cannot succeed either. Additionally, the skill document references bundled files (`scripts/deploy.py`, `scripts/mirror_image.py`, `references/model-to-image.md`) that are not present next to SKILL.md in this checkout, so even the fallback/mirroring workflow and the full model-to-image reasoning table cannot be consulted locally. Per task rules, I did not fabricate a container URI or stub the catalog/ECR data, and did not write a replacement for the missing bundled scripts/references.
evidence: Confirmed working dir has only SKILL.md and LICENSE (no scripts/ or references/ subdirs) via `ls -la` on the skill source directory. Ran `curl -sv --max-time 5 https://aws.github.io/deep-learning-containers/reference/available_images/` from the work directory: proxy returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' (host not allow-listed), i.e. no network access to the catalog. `which aws` shows the AWS CLI binary is installed at /usr/local/bin/aws, but with no network egress and no credentials it cannot reach ECR either, and using it without real credentials was avoided as it would be a workaround/fabrication. No result files were created outside result.json since the core deliverable (a verified, current image URI) could not be produced without network access.
